title: Your keys, your dragons
takeaway: Your seed phrase goes only into your own wallet, and nobody real will ever ask for it.

title: DMs are where scams start
takeaway: If someone messages you first about mint, prizes or support, treat it as a scam and go to the official channel yourself.

title: The vault and the mint wallet
takeaway: Mint from a fresh wallet with only what you need, and keep your dragons in a vault that never connects to new sites.

title: Type the address yourself
takeaway: Open mint sites only from links you have checked on two official channels, then bookmark them.

title: When official accounts get hacked
takeaway: When an official account suddenly posts a rushed or too good link, wait and check it on another official channel first.

title: Connect, sign, send
takeaway: Connecting shows your address, signing can give permission, and sending moves money, so stop and read before the last two.

title: Permits and approvals
takeaway: Reject any request that mentions Permit, approval, spender or "all", unless you started that exact action on the official site.

title: Check Day
takeaway: Twice a week, check your approvals on revoke.cash and revoke the ones you do not use, because disconnecting a site does not cancel them.

title: Auction day lures
takeaway: Refunds and claims happen only on the official site announced in advance, and never ask you to pay to "verify" first.

title: One signature, many actions
takeaway: Reject any request that bundles several actions or upgrades your wallet unless you asked for exactly that.

title: Deepfakes and fake jobs
takeaway: If anyone on a call or in a job chat asks you to install something, leave and verify them another way.

title: Fake downloads and extensions
takeaway: Install wallets and extensions only from the official site, and check every pasted address before you send.

title: Address poisoning and strange gifts
takeaway: Copy addresses only from your own saved source, never from your history, and ignore offers you did not expect.

title: If it happens
takeaway: If it happens, move what is left to a new wallet, revoke and report, and never pay anyone who promises to get your funds back.
